title: Continuity and differentiability of Thomae functions
statement: For \(T_\alpha(p/q)=q^{-\alpha}\) in lowest terms and \(T_\alpha(x)=0\) for irrational \(x\), determine continuity and differentiability, including \(\alpha=1\).
status: As of November 2026, this is a solved classical exercise. For \(\alpha>0\), continuity holds exactly at irrational points; for \(\alpha\leq0\) there are no continuity points. For \(0<\alpha\leq2\) there are no differentiability points. For \(\alpha>2\), at an irrational point with convergent denominators \(q_k\), differentiability is equivalent to \(q_{k+1}/q_k^{\alpha-1}\to0\), and the derivative is zero. The criterion is supplied by the elementary convergent estimate in the companion; \citet{varona2009differentiability} documents the classical general-power problem and its earlier literature.

title: A single continuous-function limit for the Dirichlet function
statement: Can the indicator of the rational numbers on \(\mathbb R\), already expressed by an iterated pointwise limit in the notes, be the pointwise limit of one sequence of continuous real-valued functions?
status: As of November 2026, the answer is no: Baire-one real functions on \(\mathbb R\) have a dense set of continuity points, whereas this indicator is nowhere continuous. This is an application of the classical Baire criterion, read in \citet[p.173]{baire1900nouvelle}.

title: Large-frequency asymptotics of Gaussian, quartic, and sextic Fourier integrals
statement: Determine the asymptotics as \(\lambda\to+\infty\) of \(\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-x^p}\cos(\lambda x)\,dx\) for \(p=2,4,6\).
status: As of November 2026, this is a solved steepest-descent exercise. The Gaussian is \(\sqrt\pi e^{-\lambda^2/4}\); the higher powers have exponentially damped oscillatory leading terms from a conjugate pair of dominant saddles, explicitly reconstructed in the occurrence. The method and branch convention are checked against \citet[\S2.4(iv)]{nist2026dlmf}. No new asymptotic theorem is claimed.

title: Isomorphic cohomology without a direct chain map
statement: Find complexes with isomorphic cohomology for which a prescribed cohomology isomorphism cannot be induced by a chain map in the stated direction.
status: As of November 2026, this is a solved exercise: \(A=(\mathbb Z/2)[0]\) and \(B=[\mathbb Z\xrightarrow{2}\mathbb Z]\) in degrees \(-1,0\) have the same cohomology, but every map \(A\to B\) is zero. Their derived-category isomorphism is represented by the reverse quasi-isomorphism, inverted by localization. Earlier occurrence 1971-266.3 concerns the general derived-category universal property, not the exact counterexample question, so its problem identifier is not reused.

title: Genus from a Newton polygon
statement: Determine the genus of the smooth projective model of a generic irreducible plane Laurent curve with prescribed two-dimensional Newton polygon.
status: As of November 2026, the problem is solved under Newton nondegeneracy: the genus is the number of interior lattice points. Khovanskii's 1978 publication predates this exposition; the question is a motivating problem, not an open 1981 conjecture.

title: Root counts from prescribed Newton polytopes
statement: For a generic square system of Laurent polynomials with prescribed Newton polytopes, determine the number of roots in the algebraic torus, with multiplicity.
status: As of November 2026, Bernshtein's 1975 theorem gives \(n!\) times ordinary mixed volume, with equality under the appropriate initial-system nondegeneracy. The notebook presents a problem already solved before this lecture. Earlier local Newton-polyhedron questions are related but not exact recurrences.

title: Newton-type asymptotic root count for complex exponential sums
statement: Extend the Laurent-polynomial root count to the density of roots of a regular square system of finite exponential sums with complex spectra.
status: As of November 2026, this formulation is solved by Kazarnovskii's 1981 regular-system theorem, with leading coefficient \(\kappa_n n!P_n/(2\pi)^n\) and remainder \(O(R^{n-1})\). The theorem requires its face-system regularity; arbitrary fixed systems are outside the assertion.

title: Relating exponential zero density to the growth indicatrix
statement: Explain how the exponential-sum zero-density theorem is expressed through the support functions of the spectral convex bodies, as asked by I. M. Gelfand on 2 March 1981.
status: As of November 2026, the finite-spectrum connection is established through the mixed Monge--Ampère integral already in \citet[\S1(c)]{kazarnovskii1981zeros}. \citet{kazarnovskii2024distribution} extends this framework to averaged zero currents of regular finite-dimensional spaces of entire functions of exponential growth. The later result is not a universal fixed-system convergence theorem, and the notebook does not specify such a conjecture.
